analysis:
The PR changes only docs/provider/cli-reference.md, with two edits. No code, keys, authorization or encryption paths change.

1) Head lines ~444-448 (patch hunk @@ -441 +441) describe a drain behaviour: the drain may complete without the coordinator acknowledgement only when no work is left and the provider has no registered coordinator session (for example while reconnecting). In that case the command reports 'not needed (no coordinator connection)'. A registered session must still acknowledge before the deadline. This is documentation of provider-side lifecycle behaviour. The actual implementation (ProviderLoop+Lifecycle.swift performLifecycleDrain) is not in the supplied evidence. The behaviour stays fail-closed for registered sessions. The relaxed path matters to T-053/T-010-style settlement and availability concerns only if the code skips the acknowledgement while a session is registered. That cannot be verified here, so a later pass should confirm that the unacknowledged path cannot be triggered with a live registered session, which could drop usage or settlement barriers.

2) A new runtime-constants row (patch near base ~1967-1970; head ~1974) documents a 30 s coordinator handshake deadline covering TCP, TLS and the WebSocket upgrade up to .ready. A stalled handshake is cancelled and retried with the existing backoff. This is availability-positive for TB-002. The source file CoordinatorConnectionHandshake.swift is not supplied, so I cannot confirm the implementation. It does not appear to weaken TLS or attestation.

The docs describe no new attack surface and no invalidated threat-model assumption. Reviewed base lines 1728-2005, which are context only, and head lines 1-396. The other changed hunk lines in head are outside the supplied excerpt (head 1974 is not shown). The only open question is whether the code matches the documented drain and handshake behaviour.
